name: Munich
meta_description: TDSC investigative consulting in matters touching Munich: supply chain and board disputes, automotive and tech due diligence, and IP-related research.
hero_lede: Investigative consulting for matters connected to Munich: due diligence on automotive, technology, insurance and life sciences counterparties, fact development for supply chain and boardroom disputes before the English-capable Munich Commercial Court, and asset research. Scoped from Nashville with qualified German professionals and counsel.
intro: Munich is the capital of Bavaria and one of Germany's strongest regional economies. According to the city's economic development department, eight of Bavaria's eleven DAX companies are based in Munich and its surrounding area, together representing roughly a third of the DAX's market capitalisation as of April 2026, and purchasing power per inhabitant runs about 35 percent above the federal average. The city promotes clusters in information and communication technology, automotive and mobility, life sciences, green economy, finance and insurance, and the creative industries. Around 150,000 students, three major universities and more than 100 foreign diplomatic missions add to an international, engineering-heavy business community, served by Munich Airport.

Organisations commission investigative work connected to Munich because its industrial groups sit at the top of long international supply chains and its insurers, technology firms and start-ups attract cross-border capital. Typical triggers include due diligence on suppliers, distributors and acquisition targets in the automotive, engineering and technology sectors; background research on management and supervisory board members; fact development for supply chain, warranty and director liability disputes, which since June 2025 can be brought before a specialised commercial court in Munich; research on intellectual property infringers and counterfeit networks; and asset tracing to support enforcement against Bavarian companies or individuals.

matters.title: Supplier and supply chain due diligence
matters.text: Ownership, financial standing and litigation history of suppliers, sub-suppliers and distributors linked to Munich automotive and engineering groups, including research relevant to German supply chain due diligence expectations on human rights and environmental standards, to support onboarding, audits and disputes.

matters.title: Board and executive liability disputes
matters.text: Fact development and background research for disputes between companies and members of their management or supervisory boards, a category the Munich Commercial Court now hears, including chronologies of decisions, related-party links and outside business interests, structured with German counsel.

matters.title: Technology and start-up investment checks
matters.text: Background research on founders, investors and shareholders of Munich technology, deep-tech and life sciences companies ahead of venture, growth or acquisition investments, covering commercial register history, prior ventures, insolvencies, litigation, related-party links and reputation in Germany and abroad.

matters.title: Intellectual property and counterfeit research
matters.text: Open-source and corporate research identifying the entities, owners and distribution channels behind suspected infringement or counterfeit products, to support Munich-based rights holders and their counsel in patent, trademark and trade secret matters and in enforcement planning.

matters.title: Insurance and financial fraud inquiries
matters.text: Support to insurers, reinsurers and counsel examining suspected claims fraud, misrepresentation or misconduct involving Munich-based carriers or policyholders, focusing on corporate links, asset indicators and public court records rather than any access to confidential supervisory or police data.

local_context.title: Munich Commercial Court
local_context.text: Since 1 June 2025 two civil senates of the Higher Regional Court Munich sit as a Commercial Court under the 2024 federal act strengthening Germany as a place of justice. The 40th senate hears supply chain disputes between companies, including ESG and human rights standard issues; the 41st hears disputes between companies and board members. Claims must be worth at least 500,000 euros, proceedings can be held in English, and parties reach the court by agreement, unobjected appearance or referral from a regional court.

local_context.title: Confidentiality and appeals
local_context.text: According to published commentary, the Munich Commercial Court can classify information as confidential, limit third-party file access and restrict access to hearings and documents, and its judgments can be appealed directly to the Federal Court of Justice. Its jurisdiction extends to the Bamberg and Nuremberg court districts. Investigative findings intended for these proceedings should be prepared with counsel so that sources and confidentiality designations are handled correctly.

local_context.title: Courts and commercial register
local_context.text: Ordinary commercial litigation in the city goes to the Regional Court Munich I, with appeals to the Higher Regional Court Munich. The commercial register for companies seated in Munich is kept by the Local Court Munich and is searchable through the joint register portal of the German states described on the Germany country page. Munich is also home to German and European patent institutions relevant to IP disputes.

local_context.title: Bavarian data protection supervision
local_context.text: Bavaria splits data protection supervision by sector. The Bavarian State Office for Data Protection Supervision in Ansbach supervises companies and other private bodies headquartered in Bavaria, while the Bavarian State Commissioner for Data Protection in Munich covers Bavarian public authorities and municipalities. Internal investigations at Munich employers should therefore be planned with the Ansbach authority's guidance, the data protection officer and works council arrangements in mind.

tdsc_approach: For matters touching Munich, TDSC first maps where the dispute or transaction is likely to be decided, because the Munich Commercial Court's supply chain and board liability remit, its English-language option and its confidentiality tools shape what evidence counsel will need. Research draws on the commercial register, published financial statements, court and insolvency records, patent and trademark registers and open sources, reviewed under the GDPR and German data protection law, with the Bavarian private-sector supervisor's expectations in mind for employee data. Where interviews, site checks or fieldwork in Bavaria are needed, TDSC coordinates qualified German investigators operating under the applicable trade rules. TDSC has no office in Munich.

faqs.q: What kinds of disputes does the Munich Commercial Court hear?
faqs.a: Since June 2025 it hears, at first instance, supply chain disputes between companies, including warranty and ESG standard issues, and disputes between companies and members of their management or supervisory boards, where the value is at least 500,000 euros. Proceedings can be held in English. Counsel decides whether a matter qualifies; TDSC aligns its fact work with that choice.

faqs.q: Can TDSC support supply chain due diligence for a Munich manufacturer?
faqs.a: Yes, within lawful research limits. TDSC examines ownership, management, litigation, sanctions exposure and reputation of suppliers and intermediaries, and identifies indicators relevant to human rights and environmental risk. It does not perform audits requiring accreditation, and site visits are coordinated with licensed local professionals where the supplier is located.

faqs.q: Which data protection authority supervises a Munich employer?
faqs.a: Private companies headquartered in Bavaria are supervised by the Bavarian State Office for Data Protection Supervision, based in Ansbach, not Munich. The State Commissioner in Munich covers public bodies. TDSC plans employee-related research with counsel and the data protection officer and limits the personal data gathered to the agreed purpose.

faqs.q: Can investigative findings be kept confidential in Munich proceedings?
faqs.a: The Munich Commercial Court can, on application, classify information as confidential and restrict file access and hearing attendance. Whether to seek this is a decision for the client's counsel. TDSC prepares reports with clear sourcing so counsel can decide what to disclose and what to protect.

faqs.q: Does TDSC have staff in Munich?
faqs.a: No. TDSC has no office, staff or address in Munich or elsewhere in Germany. Engagements are scoped and managed from Nashville. Where local inquiries are required, TDSC coordinates independent German investigators and works with the client's German counsel under a written scope agreed in advance.
